info.title: Building58 relay
info.description: The relay passes commands to a world's page and runs the room: tickets, tasks, sessions and reviews. It answers this computer only. Each route's description is the manual's, from docs/manual/relay.html, where the fields, the tokens and the errors are.

servers.description: The relay on this computer. npm run office starts it on 8787.

parameters.description: The channel, such as office: 1 to 64 letters, numbers, dashes or underscores.

requestBody.description: JSON. The fields are in the description.

get.description:
What the Lead sees of the Floor, and each session's desk: ticket, title, column, pr, ciWords, review, doing, next (text and owner) and stop (safe and reason). The Lead's row also has tired, and every other row has null there. A Dev's row has waitsOn while the PR watch is on and its task has an open PR: owner, minutes, why, late and words. Every other row has null there. Each row has seat: lead for the Lead, pm for the PM the room keeps running (the PM's seat), and null for the rest. A Dev's desk has rounds, how many times its PR was reviewed. The answer also has pm: trust (the rung, 0 to 4), trustName, sortHours and nextSortAt, the time the PM next sorts the Board, or null when it does not. See What the Lead sees and What each desk says.

Tokens: the relay key, and the token of the Lead. A route a token reaches can still refuse it, as the description says.

From docs/manual/relay.html#routes.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: The channel, such as office: 1 to 64 letters, numbers, dashes or underscores.

post.description:
With a session's token, {"who"}: the Lead stops one session. Only the token of a Lead you let move the board, and only while Let the Lead stop sessions is on (or RELAY_LEAD_STOPS=1). See What the Lead stops. With the relay key, as the page sends it, {"who": terminal id} or {"all": true}: you stop one desk, or every desk, that its desk calls safe to stop at that moment. The Lead's desk is never safe to stop. GET /floor also gives leadEnded: null while a Lead runs or nothing is offered back, or, once the Lead's session ended in this run, how it ended (stopped, ended or crashed) and a sentence that says so. One that is not safe is refused with not_safe and the reason. See What each desk says.

Tokens: the relay key, and the token of a Lead you let move the board. A route a token reaches can still refuse it, as the description says.

requestBody.description: JSON. The fields are in the description.

post.description:
Only with the relay key, and only from the room page on this computer: a session's token gets 403 person_only. Writes one jam you fixed by hand, {"kind", "fix", "ticket", "pr", "since", "by"}. kind is one of no-first-review, desks-full, news-untold, handed-over, waits-on-state, person-merge, merged-not-done, no-new-commit, main-red, signing-key, workflows-push, dev-idle, tunnel-down or other, and fix is one line of up to 200 characters. ticket and pr are ids with no spaces, since is when it got stuck (an ISO time, not in the future and not over 90 days ago), and by is you unless given. Anything else is 400 bad_param. See The jam log.

Tokens: the relay key only.

From docs/manual/relay.html#routes.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: The channel, such as office: 1 to 64 letters, numbers, dashes or underscores.

get.description:
Only with the relay key, and only from the room page on this computer: a session's token gets 403 person_only. ?range=1d|7d|30d (7d by default, anything else is 400 bad_param) lists the jams logged in the range, oldest first, each with at (when it was logged), kind, ticket, pr, since, fix and by, and kinds gives each kind's name. See The jam log.

Tokens: the relay key only.

parameters.name: channel

get.description:
Only with the relay key. What the manager's watch found: on, how often it looks (every, seconds), how many times it has looked (looks) and when (lastLook), its limits, the checks it counts (pr, name and the commits that check failed on), the problems that open now (key, since and the ticket it filed), and its last notes: seq, at, kind, ticket, task, terminal, reason, say and the ticket it filed.

Tokens: the relay key only.

From docs/manual/relay.html#routes.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: The channel, such as office: 1 to 64 letters, numbers, dashes or underscores.

get.description:
Only with the relay key, and only from the room page on this computer. The numbers behind the Metrics page. ?range= is 1d, 7d (the default) or 30d, and anything else is 400 bad_param. ?format=csv answers the same numbers as CSV, with the columns chart, when, label, series and value, as a download. The JSON has numbers (merged, medianMinutes, waitingOnYouHours, stalledHours, noHelpShare), and one part for each chart: merged, perTicket, where, outcomes, stalls, waits, rounds, desks, load and pm. It holds only ids, times, counts, states and reason words: no ticket title or body, no prompt and no key.

Tokens: the relay key only.

parameters.description: The channel, such as office: 1 to 64 letters, numbers, dashes or underscores.

A task's prMerged says the same for its card. Calls neither gh nor git. See Needs you.

Tokens: the relay key only.

post.description:
{"pr", "head", "text"}: marks a PR ready to merge. Only the Lead's token, or the relay key. The relay checks the PR with gh, posts one comment headed Ready to merge, adds the ready to merge label, and takes the label off when a new commit lands. A PR that fails a check gets 409 and not_ready, a note with a part missing gets 400, and a gh failure gets 502. See Ready to merge.

Tokens: the relay key, and the token of the Lead. A route a token reaches can still refuse it, as the description says.

List the tickets, in Board order: open tickets high, normal, low, in work order (rank) within each, then done and rejected ones, the latest changed first. It also has kinds (the kinds a ticket can have, see Kind), labels (the labels tickets have, A to Z, see Labels), wipLimit, leadStarts (the number you let the Lead start tickets up to, or 0) and leadStartsLeft. A ticket has approvedBy (you or Lead) once it is put in Ready. The room page gets the same list as a tickets event on its GET /stream when it opens the stream with board=1, with people, who sits on each ticket, and without the time each pipeline was checked. The stream's hello says whether it will (tickets). It is sent once as the stream opens, then only when it changes, and only to the room page on this computer.

post.description:
{"answer", "of", "why"}: the PM's answer to the check before Autopilot starts a ticket in Triage or Ready. answer is start, first, not-needed, duplicate or part-of. first, duplicate and part-of need of, another ticket's id, and the other two take none. why is 1 to 500 characters. It adds a note and a history step to the ticket. From PM trust Hold and propose, not-needed files a close proposal and duplicate and part-of a merge proposal, and at Close and merge the relay approves it as the PM and notes it. The answer is did: advised, proposed or carried out. Only the newest PM's token reaches it, and only while PM trust is above Off: any other token, an older PM's included, and the person's key, gets 403, and so does a ticket that is starting, started, done or rejected. Refused with 400 for an answer or an of that does not fit. See The check before a start.

Tokens: the relay key, and the token of a PM. A route a token reaches can still refuse it, as the description says.

post.description:
Changes any of a ticket's fields, saved together, or none when one is refused: title (1 to 80 characters) and body (up to 8000) of a Triage or Ready ticket; priority, high, normal or low, which puts it last in that priority; kind, a word, or "" to take it away (Kind); labels, up to 5, at any status, the list replacing the one there (Labels); mark, "hold", "replaced" with an optional replacedBy, or null to clear it (On hold, replaced, and design tickets); shapes, the tickets this design ticket shapes, while it is in Triage, Ready or Started; and base, another local branch to start from. Each field keeps its own error code, such as bad_title, bad_priority, bad_kind, bad_label, bad_mark, bad_shapes, bad_base or no_base. A field the ticket's state does not allow gets 409 not_ready, or 403 for a session's token, and a title or base another open ticket in the repo has on that branch gets 409 duplicate. For the PM and the Lead, a ticket you rejected counts too, as in filing. Only the fields that differ are written: the answer's edited lists them, and has unchanged when none do. The PM and the Lead send only title, body and priority, and priority only while you let them set the order (The PM sets the order, The Lead sets priority); anything else gets 403. Any other session's token gets 403. See Editing a ticket.

Tokens: the relay key, and the token of a PM, the Lead. A route a token reaches can still refuse it, as the description says.

{"text"}: adds a note to a ticket at any status, 1 to 2000 characters after the relay cleans the text, up to 30 notes on a ticket (409 notes_full after that). A note never changes the ticket's title, body, status, priority or approval, so a Ready ticket you approved stays approved. The answer's ticket has notes, each with by (who wrote it), role (dev, reviewer, pm, lead or null), at and text. Any session's token can send it, except the COO's and the security officer's. When there is no room between two ranks, the Triage and Ready tickets of that priority are numbered again. If the store fails partway, the ranks already written are put back and the answer is 502, or 409 and store_refused when the store refused the change. Those tickets keep a new updatedAt. While it waits, update.waitedMinutes says how long it has waited and update.restartsAnywayAt when it restarts the relay even if a session is in a turn (Update waits at most). rollback says which commit failed its check, why, and which commit runs, while the relay runs the commit it went back to, or while the folder is on it after a page-only step went back. relayKey.description: The relay key, RELAY_KEY: Authorization: Bearer <key>.

relayKeyCookie.name: relay_key_<port>
relayKeyCookie.description: The cookie the room page gets from a first load with the right ?key=. It is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict. Its name is relay_key_ and then the relay's port (relay_key_8787), not literally relay_key_<port>. The relay refuses it, with 403, when the request has an Origin that is not the relay's own address.

relayKeyQuery.name: key
relayKeyQuery.description: The relay key in the address, as the page sends it.

sessionToken.description: A session's own token, OFFICE_TICKET_TOKEN. It reaches only the routes its role needs: see docs/manual/relay.html#tokens.

error.description: A short code, such as bad_param, forbidden or not_found.

message.description: What went wrong, in plain words.

TicketStep.description: One step in a ticket's history.

by.description: Who wrote it, as the relay named them.

role.description: dev, reviewer, pm, lead or null for the person.

TicketNote.description: A note a session added to a ticket. It is not part of the ticket's body.

id.description: Such as T-5, or the issue number in the GitHub store.

rank.description: Its place in the work order within its priority.

base.description: The branch a start makes its branch from.

heldBack.description: Why nothing starts it by itself: a hold, a replacement, a design ticket or a proposal.

repo.description: The folder of the repo. A session files in its own folder, and this is ignored.

labels.description: A list, or one string with commas between.

examples.title: Flaky test in tasks.test.js
examples.body: It fails about one run in ten on CI.

examples.text: The cause is in relay/tickets.js, not relay/tasks.js. Run npm test first.

priority.description: A PM or the Lead needs its switch on to send this.

labels.description: The person only. A list, or one string with commas between.

mark.description: The person only. null or an empty string clears it.

replacedBy.description: With "mark": "replaced": the ticket that replaces it.

base.description: The person only. A local branch with commits.

TicketEdit.description: Any of these, saved together, or none when one is refused. A PM or the Lead sends only title, body and priority.

examples.title: Flaky test in tasks.test.js on CI

Task.description: A session's token gets only id, state, title, branch and pr.

examples.title: Fix the flaky test in tasks.test.js
examples.brief: Find why it fails about one run in ten on CI, and fix it.

examples.note: The PR is open for review.

state.description: working, waiting, idle, quiet or stuck, from its hooks.

seat.description: lead for the Lead, pm for the PM the room keeps running, or null.

ticket.description: Optional: the ticket, such as T-5.

since.description: Optional: when it got stuck, an ISO time.

by.description: Optional: who fixed it. you by default.

action.description: A command of the world, such as say or idle. GET /channels/{channel} lists them as unknown_action does.

wait.description: false sends it and answers at once with its id.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait, 1 to 120, 30 by default.

Command.description: The command, with the fields its action takes.

rseq.description: The relay's number for it, for ?since=.

Problem.description: Refused. 400 for a bad body, 401 for no key, 403 for a key or token that may not, 404 for an unknown route or id, 409 for a state that does not allow it, 413 for a body over 256 KB, 429 for too soon, 503 and 504 when no page answers.
